title: Vegetarian / Vegan Hot and Sour Soup
description: Vegetarian and Vegan Hot and Sour Soup is a rich, aromatic plant-based interpretation of the classic Chinese soup. A deeply savory kombu and shiitake stock is combined with wood ear mushrooms, shiitake, bamboo shoots, and tofu, then balanced with black vinegar, white pepper, soy sauce, and optional chili oil. A soy milk and cornstarch mixture can create delicate vegan egg-style ribbons while maintaining a silky restaurant-quality texture.

ingredients.title: For the Broth Base
items: Wood ear mushrooms – ½ cup, rehydrated and thinly sliced
Shiitake mushrooms – ½ cup, fresh or reconstituted and thinly sliced
Silken or medium tofu – 200 g, cut into thin strips

ingredients.title: For the Aromatics & Seasoning
items: Light soy sauce – 2 tbsp (or tamari for gluten-free preparation)
Shaoxing wine – 1 tbsp (or dry sherry, optional)
White pepper – ½ tsp, freshly ground, adjusted to taste
Chinese black vinegar – 3 tbsp (Chinkiang preferred, adjusted to taste)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Mushroom & Kombu Stock
steps: Place 6 cups water, kombu, and dried shiitake mushrooms in a pot.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Remove the kombu after approximately 20 minutes to prevent bitterness.
Strain the stock and reserve the shiitake mushrooms for slicing.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Broth
steps: Bring the prepared mushroom and kombu stock to a gentle simmer.
Add the wood ear mushrooms, sliced shiitake mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu.
Simmer for approximately 5 minutes to allow the flavors to develop.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Seasoning the Soup
steps: Stir in light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine if using, white pepper, and Chinese black vinegar.
Taste and adjust the vinegar and white pepper until the soup has a bold, lively sweet-sour and peppery character.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Thickening the Broth
steps: Combine the cornstarch with cold water and stir until completely smooth.
Stir the slurry again immediately before adding it to the soup.
Slowly drizzle the slurry into the simmering soup while stirring continuously.
Cook briefly until the broth becomes slightly thickened, glossy, and silky.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Creating Vegan Egg Ribbons
steps: For the optional vegan egg-style finish, whisk together unsweetened soy milk and 1 tbsp cornstarch.
Reduce the soup to a gentle swirl.
Slowly drizzle the soy milk mixture into the soup while stirring lightly in one direction to create delicate ribbon-like strands.
Alternatively, omit the mixture and serve the soup without egg-style ribbons.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Final Flavor Finish
steps: Stir in sesame oil just before serving.
Add chili oil if using and adjust the seasoning one final time.
Add a small splash of additional black vinegar if more acidity is desired.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Garnishing & Serving
steps: Ladle the hot soup into serving bowls.
Top with finely sliced green onions and fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately with additional black vinegar and chili oil at the table.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as a vegetarian or vegan appetizer.
Offer extra Chinkiang black vinegar and chili oil at the table so guests can customize the flavor.
Pair with vegetable fried rice, noodles, dumplings, or other Chinese dishes.
For a fully vegan preparation, ensure the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and all other packaged ingredients are confirmed vegan.

chefTips: The kombu and shiitake stock provides deep natural umami and is the foundation of the soup's flavor.
Remove the kombu after about 20 minutes to prevent the stock from becoming bitter.
Adjust the black vinegar at the end because prolonged cooking can soften its sharp acidity.
White pepper is essential for the characteristic hot flavor and provides a different heat profile from chili oil.
Add cornstarch slurry gradually so the soup becomes glossy and lightly thickened rather than gummy.
For the vegan egg ribbons, maintain a gentle swirl and drizzle the soy milk mixture slowly for delicate strands.
Add sesame oil and chili oil near the end to preserve their aroma and flavor.
